text:
arya: Heads up — we're seeing repeated east-west latency spikes between GPU nodes during peak batching windows (17:05–17:25 UTC). 95p latency goes from ~2ms to 30–120ms and packet loss shows up at 0.4–1.2% on intra-rack flows. Affected jobs are heavy-batching tensor workloads (p99 token gen impact). Anyone seen related alerts?

infra-bot: [alert] east-west-latency-spike triggered for cluster-gpu-prod (grafana: https://grafana/internal/d/EWlatency) :rotating_light:

mike: Can you paste a quick iperf3 / ping sample and ethtool output from one of the affected nodes? Also which NICs — Mellanox mlx5 or AWS ENA? Are we using RDMA for KV cache traffic?

cleo: Posting quick outputs from gpu-21 and gpu-22 (same rack).
cleo: ```
# ping -c 5 gpu-22
64 bytes from gpu-22: icmp_seq=1 ttl=64 time=32.4 ms
64 bytes from gpu-22: icmp_seq=2 ttl=64 time=28.6 ms
64 bytes from gpu-22: icmp_seq=3 ttl=64 time=34.2 ms
--- ping statistics ---
5 packets transmitted, 5 received, 0% packet loss, rtt min/avg/max = 28.6/31.2/34.2 ms

# iperf3 -c gpu-22 -u -b 10G -t 5
[  5]  0.00-5.00  sec  5.22 GBytes  8.93 Gbits/sec  0.82% loss

# ethtool -S eth0 | grep -i mtu
rx_missed_errors: 0
rx_mcast: 123

# ip link show eth0
2: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```

cleo: Note: gpu-22 shows MTU 9000, gpu-21 also 9000, but I spot some older hosts (gpu-05) in the same AZ still on 1500 — maybe drift from the recent network playbook change.

sam: kube-proxy logs spike too around that window, and CNI reported some retransmit counters increased. Could be qdisc/backpressure under heavy bursting from batching. Might not be purely MTU.

elaine: I checked dmesg on gpu-21 — saw mlx5 driver warnings around the same time: 
elaine: ```
mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: firmware error recovery found mismatch
mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: stalled completions, resetting
rdma_rxe: rxe: unexpected error -5
```

mike: That looks like RDMA flaps + possible firmware/kernel combo issue. Which kernel was rolled last week? I remember the 5.15.102->5.15.108 batch included a mlx5 fw update. If RDMA resets under load, it can cause temporary packet drops as paths reconverge.

cleo: Confirmed — nodes on the new kernel/firmware are all in rack-a and handling the biggest batch windows. Older racks (rack-c) on 1500 MTU get less throughput but more consistent latency.

mike: Short-term mitigation options:
- Move heavy-batch pods (model-serving) to racks with older kernel/firmware until we fix drivers (node-affinity override).
- Reduce batch size / shorten batching window to avoid bursting that triggers mlx5 recovery.
- As rollback: revert kernel/firmware on a small canary set and observe.
- If MTU mismatch exists across path, unify MTU to 1500 cluster-wide as quick rollback (cost: lower perf).

k8s-oncall: I'm starting a controlled drain of gpu-21 and gpu-22 and will cordon the rest of rack-a hosts flagged by infra query. Will also push a temporary taint to keep new heavy-batch pods off them. Creating ticket: INFRA-4521.

ops-svcs: Note — smaller batches will increase per-token CPU/GPU overhead and estimated token cost up ~8% for affected customers. Recommend we annotate the incident and notify a small set of affected customers (prod-only heavy users) if SLA impacted.

mike: For root cause follow-up: can infra/ML run a synthetic RDMA stress test (ib_send_bw, ib_write_bw) across the rack under controlled batch simulation and capture telemetry (dmesg, mlx logs, ethtool -S) so we can correlate the driver reset to traffic shape. Also check switch port errors and dropped packets counters on leaf switches (spine/leaf).

arya: Thanks — plan approved: k8s-oncall to isolate nodes, mike & elaIne to run canary driver rollback and synthetic tests, cleo to run MTU audit for full cluster, ops-svcs to prep customer comms if SLA thresholds hit. Please post updates in this thread. :eyes:

k8s-oncall: Updated INFRA-4521 with actions and timestamps. Drains started at 17:40 UTC.

cleo: Quick audit result: 94% of hosts MTU=9000, 6% MTU=1500. I'll push a one-shot ansible check and create remediation play to either normalize to 9000 after confirming path support, or set 1500 across the board for safety.

mike: Temporary QoS tweak idea — shape intra-node bursting on the source NIC qdisc to limit per-pod burst. Will prototype on canary nodes.

arya: Appreciate the quick triage. If we confirm mlx5 firmware/kernel regression, we should schedule a cross-team postmortem. Follow-ups in INFRA-4521. :thumbsup:
